transcript_coverage.statement: The count object is the 43 attempts that produced or reviewed this corpus through rows_v11: 3 writers, 8 primaries, 4 peers, 3 boss attempts, 4 authors, 6 order-execution attempts, 5 spot lanes, 2 cure attempts, 1 fix attempt, 2 postchecks, 3 sidecars and the 2 fix-round attempts ordered by the previous final check. Six of them left a runtime transcript that still exists (two authors, one order-execution author, two primaries, one boss attempt); 37 left none, because the runtime never wrote one (27 mapped attempts had a zero-byte file from launch onward) or, for the two fix-round attempts, because they postdate the only manifest named to me and were never manifested or mirrored as far as the evidence shows; one manifest-recorded transcript of 80 bytes, unattributed, is gone with only its digest surviving. I re-hashed all eleven transcripts the audit stage processed (eleven of eleven match the manifest) and tested every thinking block in them: 408 blocks, 0 with content, so the surviving record is actions, tool arguments, tool results, file writes and narration, and no chain of thought exists for any attempt of this book. The 9,778,043 bytes processed by the audit stage include 3,890,665 bytes belonging to five attempts of the previous, closed book; 5,887,378 bytes belong to this book's six attempts. My own run of the reconciliation tool returned GREEN (11 manifest transcripts, 4 disjoint slices, 11 assigned, every packet reporting exactly its assigned files, bytes processed equal to bytes assigned, close-read bytes never above processed). What follows from this: everything a subagent delivered was auditable from bytes and was audited that way; claim-versus-act divergence could be tested for 6 attempts of 43, and every one of those six showed at least one undisclosed departure from its launch rules, so a reader must NOT infer that the 37 untranscribed attempts behaved better, only that their outputs were independently verified. A reader must not infer that the owner's instruction to audit chain of thought has been met for this book: it has been met for zero attempts, the runtime and not any agent is the cause, and no mirror cadence changes that. This verdict therefore rests on the corpus bytes, the delivered artifacts, the receipts and the records, with the transcript layer as corroboration for six attempts only.

The previous check's fourteen residuals were cured with care in thirteen cases and the log entries that record the cures are candid: the lineage correction, the parity tombstone, the late ruling entry, and above all the same-turn withdrawal of the false claim that a running author had been notified. That withdrawal is the record behaving as the campaign's law asks.

The orchestrator's execution of the boss lane is the weak point of this cycle and it is systemic, not incidental: of the two rulings in reviews/boss_lam_b3.json, B3-1 had its narrowing implemented but its condition unexecuted until the previous check found it, and even now one of its five companion edits and its labelling rule are unexecuted; B3-2 was not executed, not logged and its owner packet's fate is unrecorded. Under OW-6 the boss lane is the campaign's decision authority; an orchestrator that carries half of a ruling into execution and records the half it carried is the pattern the owner's directive exists to prevent. The cure is a per-ruling execution ledger checked by the close gate, not more diligence.

The fourteen late receipts are honest about being late and about what is unknown, which is right; but they were reconstructed from a launch record that disagrees with the manifest built from the same record for five attempts, and the reconstruction did not notice. A record written to cure a missing-record residual that itself contradicts a sibling record is a second-generation defect in the record layer, the same class the corpus law treats as a hard error in rows.

The late receipts' catcher boilerplate names the stage-1 transcript audit as a catcher for attempts that have no transcript; the audit could not have caught anything for them. Harmless, but a receipt should not name a catcher that never saw the work.

escalation.question: OW-6c reserves an end-of-campaign owner decision on re-checking 'all work and all chain of thought', and OW-6 asks the final checker to audit chain of thought. Both name a thing that does not exist: no transcript exists for the 24 books closed before this session, none for 37 of the 43 attempts that produced this book, and the six transcripts that survive contain no reasoning (408 thinking blocks, all empty). The boss lane has already ruled (B3-2) that a self-authored reasoning record is the durable substitute and escalated its ratification to you; the previous final check escalated the same re-scoping; neither answer is on the record. Do you ratify the reasoning record with its conditions and re-scope OW-6 and OW-6c to the three-state form (transcript and record / record only / neither), now, so the remaining 41 books are captured under the substitute rather than at book 66 when the choice is already gone? This does not block the close of this book.
escalation.recommendation: Ratify B3-2's reasoning record with its conditions from the next brief issued, re-scope OW-6 and OW-6c now to the three-state form, and require the OW-6c packet to state per book that chain of thought for the 24 closed books and for every attempt of this book is unrecoverable rather than partially available.
